newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shrs seen soft in 2nd day of profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shrs seen soft in 2nd day of profit-taking.

text.p: Caracas stocks were seen slipping for a second consecutive day as a temporary liquidity squeeze prompts investors to take profits, traders said.

"A short term local liquidity squeeze could lead some investors to use profit-taking to secure cash flow," said Banesco broker Simon Brad. Interest rates in the overnight interbank market have topped 40 percent in the past few days.
"But any slippage in stocks won't be large," he added.
On Wednesday, the market's 19-share .IBC index lost 0.3 percent to close at 4,850.21 points after previously setting three record highs.
Trade volume swelled to the year's second highest level as 58 million shares, worth 15.7 billion bolivars ($33 million), exchanged hands.
Blue chips fell in Tuesday's profit-taking, though secondary shares consolidated gains. Among traded issues, 17 rose, ten fell and 10 closed flat.
